cards.explanation: The answer is judgment. Habakkuk says, "O LORD, You have appointed them to execute judgment…" (Habakkuk 1:12). He's talking about the Chaldeans, the nation the LORD said He was raising up (Habakkuk 1:6). Habakkuk gets the word right even while he's wrestling with what it means, friends.

The answer is True. Habakkuk says it right there in the middle of his prayer: "We will not die." (Habakkuk 1:12). He says it just after calling the LORD his God and his Holy One, and just before he starts asking the hard questions. I think that's a man who has a lot on his mind and still knows where to stand.

The answer is why the LORD is silent while the wicked swallow up those more righteous. Habakkuk asks, "Why are You silent while the wicked swallow up those more righteous than themselves?" (Habakkuk 1:13). He asks it straight out, with no sneaking around the question, friends. I think that's the kind of honest question a person only asks someone they trust.

The answer is a hook. "The foe pulls all of them up with a hook…" says Habakkuk 1:15. Then come the dragnet and the fishing net too. The whole picture is a fisherman's, bakers, and the people are the catch.

The answer is False. Habakkuk 1:15 says the foe pulls them up with a hook, catches them in his dragnet and gathers them in his fishing net, "so he rejoices gladly." No sorry in sight, friends. He's glad about his haul.

The answer is that he sacrifices and burns incense to his nets. Habakkuk 1:16 says, "Therefore he sacrifices to his dragnet and burns incense to his fishing net…" He treats his nets like they deserve a ceremony. The verse goes on to say that by these things his portion is sumptuous and his food is rich.

The answer is at his guard post on the ramparts. Habakkuk says, "I will stand at my guard post and station myself on the ramparts." (Habakkuk 2:1). Then he says he'll watch to see what the LORD will say to him. I think that's a man who plans to stay put until he gets an answer, friends.

The answer is False. The LORD tells Habakkuk, "Write down this vision and clearly inscribe it on tablets, so that a herald may run with it." (Habakkuk 2:2). It's to be written down clearly, and the purpose is for a herald to run with it. Nothing about keeping it to himself, bakers.

The answers are herald and run. The LORD says the vision is written "…so that a herald may run with it." (Habakkuk 2:2). A herald is someone who carries a message to others, friends. The picture is a messenger running with the message in hand, and that's why the LORD says to inscribe it clearly.

The answer is to wait for it because it will surely come. The LORD says, "Though it lingers, wait for it, since it will surely come and will not delay." (Habakkuk 2:3). It may feel slow, but the text says it will come. Waiting is hard work, friends, and I know it myself from my years waiting in the back of a dark junk drawer.

The answer is by faith. The LORD says, "…the righteous will live by faith…" (Habakkuk 2:4). It's set right beside the proud one, whose soul is not upright. Two very different people, bakers, and the verse tells you what the righteous one lives by.
